newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields close lower on foreign markets.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields close lower on foreign markets.

text.p: 1630 GMT - Swedish bond yields on Wednesday driven by firmer foreign markets and an oversubscribed nine year bond auction in Sweden. The National Debt Office received 10.43 billions in bids for a volume of two billion.
The crown strengthened against the dollar and the mark.

The market is focusing on U.S. statistics for jobless claims and on the Philadelphia Fed survey, due Thursday. * Six month T-bill rate rose by three basis points to 3.73 pct * Nine year bond yield fell by six basis points to 6.57 pct * Crown firmed to 4.3650 to mark vs 4.3700 late Tuesday.
Swedish bond yields ended several basis points lower on Wednesday but off lowest levels on stronger foreign markets.
"The market has followed foreign markets today. When they weakened, so did we. There is a tendency towards a rise in yields," one dealer said.
Nine-year bond yield fell six basis points to 6.57 percent.

Dealers said Sweden's auction of two billion crowns worth of nine-year bonds was heavily subscribed and helped keep yields down. The average accepted yield was 6.53 percent and total bids amounted to 10.43 billions.
The shorter maturities climbed a few basis points. The six month T-bill rate rose three basis points to 3.73 percent.
Dealers said as there was no domestic statistics due out on Thursday, the market was focusing on U.S. data such as the Philadelphia Fed's survey and jobless claims.
"We are also watching the exchange rates and most particularly the dollar vs the mark", one dealer said.
The crown weakened initially but was helped by a stronger Norwegian crown as well by a stronger dollar versus the mark.
The crown firmed to 4.3650 to the mark from 4.3700 late Tuesday. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
